facts.raw_span: numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over his whole body
papules began from his bilateral eyelid margins and extended to his trunk and extremities
7-year medical history of polydipsia and polyuria
central diabetes insipidus
growth retardation
hypothyroidism

reddish-brown papules, nodules, and plaques on his periocular areas, perioral areas, neck, shoulder, axillary folds, cubital fossa, wrists, palms, umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, anogenital area, popliteal fossa, and ankles
Dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis consisting of histiocytes, lymphocytes, foam cells, multinucleated giant cells, eosinophils, and hemorrhage
negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68
Reddish-brown papules and plaques on the neck
Reddish-brown papules and plaques on the umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, and genital area
Hematoxylin-eosin stain (original magnification ×100) and Hematoxylin-eosin stain (original magnification ×200)

concepts.why: The patient's granulomatous skin lesions and endocrine abnormalities, such as central diabetes insipidus and hypothyroidism, are consistent with Niemann-Pick disease, a multisystem granulomatous disease.
The patient's skin lesions and granulomatous infiltrate are consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis, a multisystem granulomatous disease.
The patient's central diabetes insipidus, hypothyroidism, and growth retardation are consistent with Gaucher disease, a genetic disorder.
The patient's skin lesions and granulomatous infiltrate are consistent with Hand-Schüller-Christian disease, a multisystem granulomatous disease.
The patient's central diabetes insipidus, hypothyroidism, and polydipsia are consistent with autoimmune polyendocrinopathy, an autoimmune disorder.
The patient's growth retardation and hypothyroidism are consistent with congenital adrenal hyperplasia, a genetic disorder.
The patient's skin lesions and granulomatous infiltrate are consistent with histiocytosis, a multisystem granulomatous disease.
The patient's skin lesions and systemic symptoms are consistent with multisystem inflammatory disease, an autoimmune disorder.

rationales.F01: The presence of numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the whole body is more typical of Niemann-Pick disease.
rationales.F04: Central diabetes insipidus is a strong indicator of Niemann-Pick disease and less commonly associated with other listed conditions.
rationales.F08: The dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis is more characteristic of Niemann-Pick disease.
rationales.F09: The immunohistochemical results, particularly the positivity for CD68, support Niemann-Pick disease over other conditions listed.
